name: 2001 Prairie Avenue: the brick stable on the alley at 20th Street, K12
aka: the stable behind 2001 Prairie, on 20th Street

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The draft's claim, kept: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Nothing else read dates it, so the range claims the 1904 target and no more. TO is the last day of the year the sheet was published, the latest date anything here shows it standing; it is not a demolition date.

placement.position_note: The middle of the building's alley (east) wall at grade, read off the committed sheet 35 raster (chicago/reference/prairie-avenue/sanborn-1911-and-robinson-1886/sanborn_1911_vol3_sheet_35.jpg) at pixel (1166.55, 293.085): the alley wall by a median darkness profile over rows 280-300 (peak at column 1166.55; the alley line itself reads 1171.89 on the same profile, 5.34 pixels further east, so the wall stands 0.99 m inside it), halfway between the north wall line of the building's alley end (row 275.17, a profile over columns 1115-1160) and the south wall line (row 311.00, columns 1090-1160, the 2001/2003 lot line), each peak refined by a parabola through the three highest samples. Carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_35_gcps.json): local E 1468.827, N -3485.915. The bearing is the parcel's (prairie_2001, data/street_grid/1904.json, -0.601 degrees, the draft's 179.399 less the half turn its plan frame took). The fit's own residual, 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of reading on this coarse copy, is all that is claimed. The draft had stood its corner 3.2 m north of this wall's middle, its fitted 16.25 x 6.25 m rectangle turned the other way.
placement.symbolic_location: 2001 S. Prairie Avenue, rear: east side of Prairie Avenue at the corner of 20th Street, parcel prairie_2001 (data/street_grid/1904.json); at the back of the lot, its alley wall 0.99 m inside the alley's west line and its south wall on the 2001/2003 lot line (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).

footprint.note: About the middle of the alley wall, u east (toward the alley, so the building lies at negative u) and v north. The sheet draws the building from its alley wall (pixel column 1166.55) back to its west wall (column 1080.07, a profile over rows 280-300): 86.48 pixels at the sheet's 0.185854 m a pixel, 16.073 m; and, at the alley end, from its north wall line (row 275.17) to its south wall line (row 311.00): 35.83 pixels, 6.659 m along the alley. Built as that rectangle. The sheet's north wall steps at column 1121.1 (a profile over rows 271-274): west of the step it stands on the 20th Street line (row 269.86, a profile over columns 1085-1105; the street line reads 269.96 over columns 1115-1160), so the building's west 7.63 m is 7.65 m wide; that 0.99 m strip is not built (liberty L-k12-2001-stable-1938).

stories.note: '2' lettered in the building's north-west corner, inside its west wall line. Built as the kit's carriage room (3.6 m) under a loft whose walls rise 2.7 m more to the eave, under a 30-degree roof (4.64 m from eave to ridge over the 16.07 m span); those heights are RECONSTRUCTED. No dormer: the sheet draws none and the kit builds none.

construction.note: Drawn pink, the sheet's colour for brick. The small figures written inside its north and south wall lines are too coarse on this copy to read as wall thicknesses; the kit builds its own 13-inch walls.

value.note: Everything but the plan, the two storeys and the brick is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-2001-stable-1938. The sheet gives the outline, '2' storeys, the brick, the label GARAGE, the south wall on the 2001/2003 lot line, the alley wall 0.99 m inside the alley line, and a north wall that steps: the west 7.63 m of the building stands on the 20th Street line, the east 8.45 m (the alley end) 0.99 m back from it. The kit builds a rectangle, so the building is built at its alley end's width, 6.66 m, the whole 16.07 m depth; the west part's extra 0.99 m strip along 20th Street is not built (in the liberty). The alley is on the EAST, so the kit is turned to face it (alley_side east), not mirrored, so that its party wall stands at the south end on the 2001/2003 lot line (2003's back lot is open ground on the sheet) and the open gable faces north onto 20th Street across the 0.99 m strip. On the alley wall, counted from the party wall's inner face: a carriage bay (3.0 m clear) with the loft hatch and hoist over it, and a man door with a loft sash over it. On the yard wall, counted from the gable end, a stable sash and loft sash, a door where the walk from the house meets it, and a second stable sash and loft sash. On the street gable, counted from the alley face, three stable sash and two loft sash between them: the one face of the building seen from a public street, given light as a stable's long side is. The roof is the kit's gable with the ridge along the alley at 30 degrees, the pitch 1736's and 1709's deep stables take (the kit's 40 degrees over a 16.07 m span would stand a roof 6.7 m tall on 6.3 m of wall), 4.64 m from eave to ridge; no dormer and no ventilator, as the sheet draws none. The workyard is paved from the yard door 11.16 m west to the house's rear wall (sheet column 1020). No ramp, stair, lean-to, wing or range: the sheet draws none.

coach_house.note: The building's dimensions are the footprint's (inferred, above); its openings, roof and loft are the kit's, laid out for this lot, and RECONSTRUCTED. See the value's own note for each choice and what bounds it.

function.note: Sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn draws a two-storey brick building at the back of 2001's corner lot, on 20th Street and the alley, uncrossed, and letters it GARAGE. GARAGE is the 1911 sheet's word and is not read as the 1904 use (the K12 kit's restriction no_1911_use_labels; T-1837 study ruling 11; the T-1842 census row s35-2001-rear, whose own note backcasts the envelope and reconstructs the use as a stable/coach house). This record builds it as the house's stable and coach house: a carriage bay, a loft with its hatch and hoist, stable sash, and no motor-garage part. The use is RECONSTRUCTED; no source read names a horse, a carriage or a motor car on this lot.

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 35.
what_it_supplies: Footprints, lots and street widths from 20th to 22nd Street between Indiana and Calumet, as of 1911, at the copy's coarser resolution
The position of Twentieth Street, which is vacated between Indiana and Calumet today
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
Any lake edge: the sheet ends at Calumet Avenue

research_note: T-1938 refines the district draft (T-2352) in place under the same id onto the K12 coach-house kit, the second of the package's alley buildings on the east side of Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street, to leave the draft (2027's barn was the first). The sheet census (census row s35-2001-rear, trace s35fp-2001-b2) carries the building into 1904; the draft rules now skip that row. Read afresh off the committed sheet 35 raster by median darkness profiles rather than taken from the draft's fitted rectangle (16.25 x 6.25 m inside 89% of the trace): the sheet draws a building 16.07 m deep from its alley wall and, at that alley end, 6.66 m along the alley, its south wall on the 2001/2003 lot line; the north wall stands on the 20th Street line for the building's west 7.63 m and 0.99 m back from it for the east 8.45 m, and the alley wall stands 0.99 m inside the alley line, so the corner of 20th Street and the alley is left clear. This copy of the sheet is coarse (0.186 m a pixel), so every reading here carries about a pixel. Nothing read dates the building before the 1911 sheet; that it stood by 1904 is the census's carry-back, which the district draft already made. No picture of the alley behind the 2000 block is known to this project.
